text:
amanda (PM): quick thread — I sketched a proposal for a lease-exchange flow: let customers convert a portion of their reserved pool into short-lived burst credits. idea is to give predictable baseline + optional burst capacity customers can buy/use on top without a separate addon SKU. gating would be by SLO tier + per-tenant preemption budget. thoughts?

raj (Eng): curious about gating rules. is this an override of autoscale or a separate admission control?

amanda (PM): separate admission control layer. baseline stays same. burst credits are drawn from a tenant bucket, router checks: 1) tenant has credits, 2) current pool utilization < soft_threshold OR route allowed to spill. if both true -> admit as burst lane. else -> fallback to lower-qa model or throttle.

maya (Eng-Platform): rough config idea:
```
burst_policy: 
  soft_threshold_pct: 75
  max_burst_per_min: 2000
  credit_decay: 1h
  preempt_policy: evict-oldest
  allowed_slo_classes: [platinum, gold]
```
will need router + admission changes and new credit accounting table.

leo (SRE): we need clear degradation windows. preempt-policy evict-oldest sounds ok but we must surface when tenants are using burst credits (alerts + dashboard). don't want noisy noisy evictions during peak.

nicole (CSE): major customers keep asking for burst guarantees but want price predictability. if we expose a lease-exchange, they expect a contract/legal language that maps credits -> uptime/latency. recommend default: credits only usable for best-effort, with an opt-in SLA addon for guaranteed bursts.

jordan (Sales): +1. Sales will want a simple tradeoff grid for contracts: e.g., convert 10% reserved -> +X burst credits/month at Y price. also need messaging for enterprise that uses dedicated for latency-critical workloads.

raj (Eng): implementation concerns: 1) accounting at high throughput (per-request debit), 2) fairness when multiple tenants spike, 3) rollback story for failed debits. we could do optimistic pre-debit in router + eventual reconciliation in billing. instrumentation required.

maya (Eng-Platform): for throughput: shard credit ledger by tenant-region and do local caches with periodic reconcile. admission check should be local cache-based for latency; reconcile in background. will add a new metric stream: burst_debits, burst_rejects, burst_preemptions.

leo (SRE): define SLOs for admission ops: <2ms added p95 for router checks and reconcile lag < 60s. create an alert if reconcile error rate > 0.1%.

amanda (PM): launch criteria proposal:
- design review approved by eng, platform, and SRE
- e2e canary with 3 pilot customers for 2 weeks
- dashboards + alerting in console (burst usage per tenant)
- legal/pricing language drafted by sales + legal
- fallback policy tested (route to lower-cost model or graceful 429 semantics)

nicole (CSE): pilot ask: pick 2 customers that already accept degraded tail latency for cost savings + 1 that wants near-zero impact and will pay for guaranteed bursts. helps validate both opt-in models.

jordan (Sales): will surface 3 pilot candidates — do we have a one-pager I can share?

amanda (PM): I'll draft one tonight and drop in #product-ops. includes pricing examples and tradeoff matrix.

raj (Eng): timeline estimate: 6 sprints to get core admission + accounting + reconcile + canary plumbing. additional 2 sprints for SLA-backed guaranteed-burst path.

maya (Eng-Platform): curious about fallback when reconcile fails — router should conservatively deny bursts if ledger state unknown. prefer safe default.

leo (SRE): agree — fail closed for bursts. also add a slowpath metric if router stalls on ledger fetch.

amanda (PM): decisions we need here:
- do we allow self-serve exchange in console or restrict to Sales/legal signoff?
- default preemption policy (evict-oldest vs fair-share)
- price model: % of reserved -> credits OR fixed add-on bundles
write answers here and we'll lock design doc on Mon.

nicole (CSE): suggest restrict GA self-serve to non-SLA bursts, require sales/legal for guaranteed bursts. simplifies billing first.

jordan (Sales): pricing preference: simple % convert -> credits with an optional prepay multiplier for discounted credits. example: convert 10% reserved -> 1.2x credit multiplier if prepay annual. customers like simple math.

raj (Eng): preemption policy: implement evict-oldest first as MVP; fair-share later. coding effort small for oldest.

amanda (PM): ok locking those for MVP: self-serve only for best-effort bursts, evict-oldest, %->credits pricing. next steps:
- @maya: sketch API + router hooks (due Thu)
- @raj: scope epic & ops playbook (due Fri)
